classification.difficultyReason: Identify two sign-change boundaries in each expression, coordinate the signs of both absolute values across three intervals, simplify the branch equations and join them into continuous sketches. The requested branch-first method is explicit; the demand lies in managing linked sign cases and graphical representations.

content.prompt: Carefully write down the equations of the branches of each function, then sketch its graph:

answer.worked:
The arguments change sign at $x=-1$ and $x=3$.
$$\begin{align*}y&=-(x+1)+(x-3)=-4 &&(x<-1),\\y&=(x+1)+(x-3)=2x-2 &&(-1\le x<3),\\y&=(x+1)-(x-3)=4 &&(x\ge3).\end{align*}$$
The branches join at $(-1,-4)$ and $(3,4)$. The intercepts are $(1,0)$ and $(0,-2)$.

spec.description: Horizontal left ray at -4, increasing segment from (-1,-4) to (3,4), horizontal right ray at 4; source guides and intercept labels retained.
